title: Remediate race between eviction and insert that caused prefix cache pointer corruption
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Summary:

During a capacity spike on 2026-02-23 we observed an increase in OOM restarts and elevated latency for text-generation routes. The post-incident trace and heap profiles point to a corruption window in the prefix cache: pointer/tombstone chains were intermittently invalidated during concurrent eviction + insert across shards, which allowed stale slab references to persist and prevented normal GC -> resulting in a slowly growing resident memory leak and occasional key-poisoning where a reader observed an incorrect prefix mapping.

Why this ticket exists:

This ticket captures the actionable follow-ups to fully remediate the root cause, reduce blast radius, and add automated checks and telemetry so we detect regressions earlier. The immediate mitigation (viewport throttling + emergency restart + disable aggressive eviction heuristics) is in PROD behind a one-off feature flag; this ticket coordinates the safe long-term fixes and verification.

Root cause (summary):

- The eviction routine uses a relaxed lock sequence per-shard to avoid tail latency, and inserts acquire per-key write fences. Under extreme concurrency the eviction and insert paths could reorder such that the eviction removed an index node while an insert re-linked a new value to the same slot without synchronizing the tombstone counter.
- This produced a transient state where a slab pointer referenced freed memory until the background sweeper ran. In fast-path cases the sweeper was backlogged and tombstones accumulated.
- A second bug in the prefix reconciliation process skipped tombstone scans for slots older than X seconds, which allowed the accumulation to continue across restarts.

Incident timeline (high level):

- 2026-02-23 14:12 UTC: first elevated OOM/restarts observed (alerts triggered).
- 2026-02-23 14:35 UTC: on-call infra disabled aggressive eviction heuristics, toggled feature flag evict-async=false, and rolled a restart of a subset of serving fleet.
- 2026-02-23 16:20 UTC: stabilization observed; memory growth plateaued for nodes with the flag.
- 2026-02-24 -> 2026-02-25: postmortem analysis and heap dumps collected; reproducer built in staging.

Action items (owner / ETA / status):

1) Implement strong ordering primitive for eviction+insert paths (lockless compare-and-swap protocol + tombstone epoch) to eliminate reordering window.
   - owner: Aisha Patel
   - estimate: 8 pts
   - due: 2026-03-12
   - status: In Progress
   - notes: prototype branch at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4839 (WIP)

2) Fix tombstone reconciliation to scan previously excluded slots and ensure sweeper idempotency across restarts.
   - owner: Jun Park
   - estimate: 3 pts
   - due: 2026-03-02
   - status: In Review
   - notes: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4846 includes new unit tests and deterministic reproducer.

3) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates high-concurrency eviction+insert workload with deterministic scheduler to catch the race.
   - owner: Priya Shah
   - estimate: 5 pts
   - due: 2026-03-08
   - status: Planned
   - notes: test should be included in CI gating for runtime-1.22 and run as a slow integration job.

4) Add telemetry and early-alerting: per-shard tombstone_count, sweeper_lag_seconds, evict_insert_conflicts, and slab_free_failures. Create Grafana dashboard and PagerDuty alert thresholds.
   - owner: SRE Team (contact: Elena Rossi)
   - estimate: 3 pts
   - due: 2026-03-05
   - status: In Progress
   - notes: dashboard mockup at https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/kv-cache/eviction-health

5) Backfill incident runbook: a concise checklist to mitigate without full restarts (feature flag toggles, safe restart order, node isolation, cache warmup steps). Update runbook and link in Oncall docs.
   - owner: Marco Nguyen
   - estimate: 2 pts
   - due: 2026-03-03
   - status: Done
   - notes: runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/KB-kv-cache-eviction-runbook

6) Soft rollout plan and canary: deploy the ordering fix behind a feature flag, canary on 2% of capacity for 48 hours with telemetry gating, then 25% for 24 hours, then full rollout.
   - owner: Release Engineering (contact: Leah Kim)
   - estimate: 1 pt (coordination)
   - due: 2026-03-16
   - status: Planned

7) Retrospective + blameless postmortem note: capture decisions, what slowed diagnosis (missing metrics for evict_insert_conflicts), and reduce cognitive load for future responders.
   - owner: Incident Lead (Marco Nguyen)
   - estimate: 2 pts
   - due: 2026-03-01
   - status: Done

Immediate mitigations already applied (summary):

- Disabled async eviction heuristics (evict-async=false) in the hottest shards.
- Scoped restart of 30% of serving fleet and promoted nodes from warm pool.
- Emergency throttling of large-batch requests on affected customer routes.

Verification plan:

- Deploy ordering fix behind FF to staging; run integration reproducer for 6 hours with contention set to extreme. Verify tombstone_count remains bounded and slab retention pattern matches baseline.
- Canary in production with 2% traffic for 48 hours; monitor evict_insert_conflicts==0, tombstone_count stable, memory RSS growth <= baseline + 5%.
- After full rollout, schedule a post-rollout heap-snapshot sweep after 72 hours to confirm no slow leak.

Risks & trade-offs:

- Stronger ordering primitives will cost additional CPU cycles on the hot path; we will micro-benchmark to choose CAS vs lightweight adaptive locks.
- Disabling async eviction permanently increases steady-state memory usage; hence the long-term fix must be implemented before reverting the mitigation flags.

Notes and links:

- Incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-02-kv-leak
- Heap dumps and flamegraphs: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/kv-leak/2026-02-23/
- Reproducer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/repro/kv-evict-insert-race
- Related tickets: ENG-26341 (incident), ENG-26900 (slab allocator defrag work), ENG-26890 (sweeper redesign)

Acceptance criteria (for closing this ticket):

- PR with ordering fix merged to main and passes CI and integration tests.
- Canary shows no evict-insert conflicts for 48h at 2% traffic and no abnormal memory growth.
- Telemetry dashboard and PDB/PagerDuty alerts created and tested.
- Runbook updated and linked in Oncall docs.
- Post-deploy heap-snapshot confirms no persistent leak across a 7-day window for affected nodes.

If any step fails during canary, the rollback plan is: immediately flip feature flag to old behavior, isolate affected nodes, and open an emergency incident call with SRE + runtime owners.

Comments and ongoing updates will be appended to this ticket as PRs and canary results land.
